text: Standard GNNs are not continuous across graph resolutions: GCN's MAE increases from 63.6±1.3 kcal/mol in same-resolution QM7 regression to 138.1±2.4 kcal/mol under cross-resolution evaluation (Table 1).

Latent embedding differences ||F-F̄|| between resolutions diverge for standard architectures, with GIN showing the worst divergence at 881.2±268.7 (high-to-low resolution) and 2875.8±1527.7 (low-to-high resolution) (Table 2).
The discontinuity arises because renormalized adjacency-matrix propagation creates disconnected effective limit graphs rather than preserving coarse-grained structure (Section 5, Figure 4a-4b).

Theorem 7.1 proves that networks using Laplace-transform propagation achieve provable scale-continuity, bounding the embedding difference by a constant times the heat-kernel convergence term (Theorem 7.1, Eq. 5).
The proposed Laplace-transform propagation reduces embedding differences across resolutions to 0.2-0.3, versus 18.0-2875.8 for standard GNN propagation schemes (Table 3).
Prediction accuracy of the modified architecture remains stable across resolutions, e.g., MPNNexp attains 17.4±3.4 MAE at same resolution versus 17.9±5.2 at cross-resolution (Table 4).
